Someone Paid Bicycle Money for This V8-Powered Mercedes CLS – No Catch Here
17 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
I asked the missus how much she thinks this car costs. And she said: “What? $30,000-$40,000?” And that’s what your non-petrolhead neighbors would have probably thought, too, if you had the chance to write your name on the dotted line of this Mercedes-Benz CLS .
However, real petrolheads know that this is a first-gen car. The C219, which was made between 2003 and 2010, was the original four-door coupe. It was based on the same platform as the era’s Mercedes E-Class (W211), and was offered with a couple of V6 units, several V8s, and a diesel, paired either with a five-speed or a seven-speed automatic transmission, depending on the specification.
This machine is a 2006 Mercedes-Benz CLS , and it is in the 500 configuration. As a result, it features a 5.0-liter V8 engine under the hood. The unit was officially rated at 302 hp (306 ps/225 kW) and 339 lb-ft (460 Nm) of torque back then, and it drives the rear axle through a seven-speed self-shifting gearbox. For something that came out two decades ago, the model needs a very respectable 6.1 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from zero.
Finished in Pewter Metallic, which definitely screams 2000s from its pores, the pictured car has a brown interior, and a clean California title. It is located in Redwood City, CA, though only for the moment, as it recently changed hands at an online auction in the United States of America.
Photo: Cars&Bids More on that topic in a few moments, as first, we have to tell you that it features air suspension, a power-operated sunroof, and 18-inch wheels. This old Mercedes-Benz CLS also has leather upholstery, wood trim, power-adjustable, heated, and ventilated front seats, a four-zone automatic climate control system, and an audio from Harman Kardon.
As for the known flaws, these include the “Service F exceeded by 139 days” message on the instrument cluster, a crack on the tachometer cover, stains on the driver’s sunshade, wear on the seats and interior touchpoints, curb rash on the wheels, and a weathered and cracked paint protection film on the front fascia, door mirror casings, and rear bumper.
The recent service history section in the online listing reveals that the tires were mounted in November 2024, at 98,895 miles (159,156 km), and that the transmission was checked, and the tires mounted and balanced in February 2024, at 93,863 miles (151,058 km). At the time of cataloging, this old Mercedes CLS had 100,800 miles (162,200 km) on the odo.
According to the ad, the seller represented the owner, who reportedly bought this Mercedes-Benz CLS back in July 2005, adding some 98,500 miles (158,500 km) since. The four-door coupe recently sold on Cars&Bids for new bicycle money, as mentioned in the title, and the price was $4,950. Would you have bought it for just under $5K?
